# Architecture

How MNML is put together: a Home Assistant integration that serves the cards, their editors and their templates and installs the theme, all built from this repository and released as one `mnml.zip`. For how the cards behave, see [How the cards work](cards.md); for how they look, [Design](design.md); for the theme, [The theme](theme.md).

## The parts

| Path                      | What                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/contract/`           | The contract (`cards.ts`, `entities.ts`, `templates.ts`) and what the cards and their users both read                                                                                                                                                          |
| `src/cards/`              | The cards, their base class, the known-key schemas, the registration and the loader; `parts/` holds what several cards share, and the pieces a large card's file is split into                                                                                 |
| `src/ha/`                 | Home Assistant in the browser: the typed `hass`, formatting, names, rules, conditions, navigation, motion, and the template parts that draw Home Assistant's own elements                                                                                      |
| `src/store/`              | The integration's template store in the browser, and the shipped families fetched on demand                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `src/editors/`            | The card editors and their description vocabulary                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `src/panel/`              | The MNML panel                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `src/templates/`          | The template engine, discovery, the shipped templates' loader, the dashboard expander                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `templates/`              | The shipped templates, one YAML file per family, and `shapes.yaml`, the slot shapes they share                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `src/home/`               | The home generator: `Home` and its parts, `build()`, `drawn()` and `problems()`                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `src/builder/`            | The dashboard builder: a plan's defaults from the home's registries, a person's slots, and the dashboard a plan makes                                                                                                                                          |
| `demo/`                   | The demo home, Joe's and Jane's, its YAML, and the throwaway instance's entities for it                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `src/build/`              | `buildBundle()`, and the command line that runs it                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `src/theme/`              | The theme's model, its mapping onto Home Assistant's variables, its contrast claims, its YAML                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `src/test/`               | The jsdom helpers and the fake Home Assistant connection the element tests use                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `tools/`                  | The throwaway Home Assistant, its look, walk and screenshot passes, the discovery corpus's snapshot of it (`corpus.ts`, `snapshot.ts`), the integration's icons, the wiki's pages, the release zip, and the interface's part of the release notes (`notes.ts`) |
| `custom_components/mnml/` | The integration, and in `www/` (built, git-ignored) everything it serves                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `tests/`                  | The integration's tests                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `entities.ts`       | The id types: `EntityId<Domain>` and one alias per domain (`LightId`, `SensorId`, ...). Also `MdiIcon`, `PopupHash`, `Subnet`, `ServiceName` (a closed union of the services the cards call) and `Corners<T>` (front left, front right, rear left, rear right)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `builder.ts`        | `Plan`, what the panel's builder keeps for a dashboard it made: its title and icon, its rooms by area, its people by `person` entity, its cars by key, its system templates, each with the slots it overrides, how its pop-ups open, and optionally each section's look (`SectionLook`: a title, an icon, and but for System a template; `lookOf()` gives a section's look with the defaults, `SECTION_LOOKS`), and optionally the sections' `order`, each once (`orderOf()` puts any left out after them, in `SECTION_ORDER`); optionally the Glances strip (`glances`, discovered, with overrides, or `spelled`); a room, person or system choice may be `spelled`, its slots alone with nothing discovered; `isPlan()`, which refuses an unknown key at every level, `isPersonId()`, and `SYSTEM_TEMPLATES`, the templates the builder offers for the System section. `tests/plans.json` holds example plans, valid and not, that `isPlan()` and the integration's schema both judge the same way                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `cards.ts`          | The configuration of every card: the public interface of MNML; see below                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `structure.ts`      | Every card's structure and every part's, once: `CARD_STRUCTURES`, by card type, and the parts (`STATE_ITEM`, `CONTROL`, `LIST_ROW` and the parts only a card holds). A structure names its keys in the order a form places them, each with its kind (`text`, `texts`, `number`, `share`, `flag`, a `choice` of values, `entity` and `entities` with their domains, `icon`, `popup`, `service`, `color`, `words`, `corners`, a `rule`, `summary`, a `part` or `parts` of another structure, and the `cards` and `slots` of the cards without a form), whether it is required, and its default where a form needs it. A part that comes in kinds is `tagged()` by its `type`, or `marked()` by a marker key, with a last kind for a value with no marker. `plain<T>()`, `tagged<T>()` and `marked<T>()` hold each structure to its interface in `cards.ts`: a key missing or extra, or required where the interface makes it optional, does not compile. `chooseVariant()` is the one choice of a kind for a value, for the cards' key check and for the editors. A structure holds no label: the cards derive their known keys from it (`src/cards/keys.ts`), and the editors their forms, with the labels of `src/editors/labels.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `interface.ts`      | `surface()`, MNML's public interface as plain sorted JSON, of the record format `FORMAT` (1), which it writes first, as `format`. It holds every card type and its keys, from `CARD_STRUCTURES` (`cardPaths()`): each key by its path, with its kind, `!` when it is required, its values in parentheses (a `choice`'s or `words`'s options, or what a flag writes when it is not `true`, `flag(device)`) and `=` its default where the structure gives one (`text = "data"`). A part's keys follow its key after a `.` (`fields.name`), a list's after `[]` (`rows[].entity`), and each kind of a part that comes in kinds is a path of its own, `tagged` or `marked`, its name in angle brackets (`controls[]<indicator>`, then `controls[]<indicator>.color`; `<otherwise>` for the kind with no marker; a header's `<name>.icon`); a card's `type` is the card's name in the record. It holds every shipped template and its slots (each its kind, with `!` when it is required, an object's fields as dotted paths, `lights.group`), every slot shape of `templates/shapes.yaml`, resolved, as dotted paths with kinds (`meter`, `meter.power`), the theme's name and the `mnml-*` variables it writes, the integration's domain, its options (the `CONF_*` of `const.py`) and its websocket commands (the `type` of each in `websocket.py`, read by `integrationOf()`, which fails when it reads fewer than `websocket.py` has `@websocket_api.websocket_command` decorators), and the keys of `Home`, `Room`, `Person`, `Car`, `System` and `SectionTitles` (the key tables of `src/home/types.ts`). `interface.json`, at the root, is the interface as last recorded: `interface.test.ts` fails while the two differ, naming each entry removed, changed (a key's or a slot's kind, required flag, values or default) or added, until `pnpm run fix:interface` records it. `compare()` makes that diff between two records, and `notes()` writes it as the Markdown of the release notes from the record a tag holds; `readSurface()` reads a record, and gives nothing for one of another format, which `notes()` then says to compare by hand |
| `interface-main.ts` | `pnpm run fix:interface`: writes `interface.json` from `surface()`, formatted by oxfmt. It is deliberately not part of `pnpm fix`, so that a change to the interface is recorded on purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `subnet.ts`         | `ipv4()` and `subnetRange()`, by which the clients card groups and validates                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `templates.ts`      | The template format's types (`Template`, with its `retired` slot paths, `SlotSpec`, `Rule`, `Kind`, `Value`) with `isTemplate()`, `isMapping()` and `isStorable()`, the shape the integration stores (a mapping `card`, `popups` a list of mappings); see [the template engine](#srctemplates-the-template-engine)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `yaml.ts`           | `toYaml()`, the YAML writer: YAML 1.1, with every string Home Assistant's loader or the panel would read as something else quoted ([The YAML writer](cards.md#the-yaml-writer)) ### The contract, `cards.ts`

- **Cards:** `TileCard`, `EntityCard`, `HeaderCard`, `HeadingCard`, `ListCard` (with `ListRow`), `AgendaCard` (with `AgendaSource`), `MessagesCard`, `ClientsCard` (with `ClientNetwork` and `ClientFields`), `ReportCard`, `WeatherCard`, `GlancesCard` (with `Glance`), `ButtonCard`, `SelectCard`, `SliderCard`, `MediaCard`, `CarPlanCard`, `PopupsCard` (with `Popup` and `LovelaceCardConfig`, any card a pop-up holds) and `TemplateCard`.
- **A tile's or header's subject** is one of two variants: a literal `name` and `icon`, with an optional `entity`; or an `entity` whose name (its device's, with `label`) and icon the card shows, where an `icon` may still override the entity's.
- **`Item`:** an entity with its name, state line, popup and controls. `EntityCard` is an `Item` with a `type` and optional nested `items`: the rows its expander reveals. `TileCard.item` is an `Item` too.
- **Controls:** `toggle`, `slider`, `select`, `service`, `nav`, `indicator`, `status`, `tyres`, `scenes`.
- **`StateItem`:** one entry of a state line. It is one of seven variants: an entity's state, an `attribute`, a literal `text`, the `minutes` of a seconds counter, a timestamp as a `relative` time, the `serial` number of the entity's device, or the entity's `name`. `icon: true` puts the state icon in front.
- **Rules:** `StateRule` (`is` / `not`); `EntityRule`, which adds the `entity` it reads; and a `status` control's rules, which add the `entities` they watch, how the tooltip names and words them (`label`, `words`), and the `color` they give.
- **`Condition`:** Lovelace's state condition, as `state_not` on an `entity`: the one form a card's `visibility` takes inside a pop-up, which the pop-up shell evaluates.

A card reads nothing the types don't declare, and a key it does not declare is an error (`src/cards/keys.ts`, below). Leave an optional key out to get its default, so the YAML reads as intent: `state` defaults to the entity's own state line on an entity card, and `when` to `{ is: ['on'] }` on a coloured control, pill or header. A list row is the exception: without `when` it is coloured whenever it is shown, so a flag's condition lives in its `show`, and a coloured value row spells its `when`.

A threshold that is a share of something says so in its name. `low_share` and `warn_share` on the `tyres` control, and `tyre_low_share` and `tyre_warn_share` on the car plan, are ratios of a tyre's target (0.9, 0.95). A list row's `low` and `critical` are absolute values in the entity's unit (20, 5 for a battery's percentage).

`cards.ts` is part of the public interface that `interface.json` records: a new key or card is a minor release; while MNML is 0.x a minor release may also rename or remove one, or change its meaning, with a line in the release notes on how to migrate ([Releases](#releases)), and from 1.0 that is a major release.

## `src/cards/`: the cards

- `register.ts` is the bundle's entry. It defines twenty elements, the seventeen cards, the pop-up shell, `mnml-slider` (the slider of the slider card and of a slider control's overlay) and `mnml-tooltip`, and lists the cards and the shell in `window.customCards`. Each of those gets its `getStubConfig()` from `stubs.ts`, and each but the pop-ups card its `getConfigElement()` from `edit.ts`. It skips a tag that is already defined, so a second copy of the bundle on one dashboard defines nothing and throws nothing.
- One file per card, named after it in kebab-case; `parts/` holds what several cards share, and the pieces a large card's file is split into.
- `keys.ts` and `schemas.ts`: a card's known keys are a `KeySchema`, which `keysOf()` derives from a structure of `src/contract/structure.ts`, a key that holds a part, a list of parts or a rule with the schema of that structure nested, and `cardKeysOf()` with the card's `type` too. `schemas.ts` holds them all: one constant per card (`HEADING_CARD`, `TILE_CARD`, ...) that the card imports, and the parts' `STATE_ITEMS`, `CONTROLS` and `LIST_ROW`. The structures are typed against `cards.ts`, so the schemas cannot drift from it. A union is checked against the one kind a value picks (`chooseVariant()`), which names only the keys that kind allows (not those it spells `never`): by its `type` for a control, and by a marker key for a state item, a glance, the select card, a header's or tile's subject and a message source. So a toggle with a `slider`, or a text with an `attribute`, is an unknown key too. `MnmlCard.setConfig()` checks a configuration against its card's schema before anything else, at every depth the schema describes, and allows the layout keys Home Assistant and card-mod add (`grid_options`, `visibility`, `view_layout`, `layout_options`, `card_mod`) at the top.

| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `base.ts`                               | `MnmlCard<C>`, the base class of every card but the pop-up shell and the template card: the key check, configuration, updates only for what the configuration names, holds and teardown, `notify()`, and the default grid size; `Host`, what a part a card draws is given; `requireString()`, `requireNumber()`, `requireList()`, `requireOneOf()` for a card's `validate()`. See [How the cards work](cards.md#lifecycle-of-a-card) |

Its ready state holds the store's own templates, with the shipped shapes they name resolved (one that names an unknown shape is kept as written, and reported on the console), and its changes. `resolvedTemplates()` gives the order a card, its editor and the panel read templates in: the home's own, a shipped one with its changes, the shipped. `knownShared()` and `onShared()`. Its ready state holds the home's own templates with the shapes they name resolved (one that cannot be resolved, for any reason, is kept as written and reported on the console, so only the cards that draw it fail), `written`, the own templates as stored, for the panel, and the changes |

## `src/editors/`: the card editors

The card editors are a file of their own, loaded the first time a card is edited ([Editing in the UI](editors.md)). Editors and panel parts are `LitElement`s; the rest draws `html` templates.

| Module                                 | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `main.ts`                              | The editors' entry: it loads `ha-form`, then defines `mnml-card-editor`, `mnml-template-card-editor`, `mnml-template-gallery`, `mnml-row-menu`, `mnml-words` and `mnml-related`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `shape.ts`                             | The vocabulary of a form: `Field`, `PlainShape` (its fields, sections, labels and help) and `ChoiceShape` (its kinds), with `checkValue()`, `cleanValue()`, `place()`, `switchVariant()`, `variantOf()` and `starter()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `cards.ts`                             | `describer()`, which makes the description of a form (a `Shape` of `shape.ts`) from a structure of `src/contract/structure.ts` and a table of labels: a field of each key, of the key's kind, a colour or service field with its list, a part with a description of its own; `DESCRIPTIONS`, every card with a form, which is every card but the pop-ups and template cards                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `labels.ts`                            | `LABELS`, by the name of each structure the editors draw: the label of the card or part and of each of its kinds, the label of a key whose humanised name reads badly, their help under the field, and its sections, the panels of its form (one, under its label, when it gives none)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `lists.ts`                             | The choices of a field the structure leaves to the editors: the services, held to `ServiceName`, the corner names, and the contract's colours                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `form.ts`                              | Home Assistant's form and back: `schemaOf()`, `formData()`, `fromForm()`, which writes only the fields the form changed, `slotsFromForm()`, which writes `null` for an emptied slot that has a default                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `draw.ts`                              | The drawing: `objectForm()`, a part or card in its sections or whole, with the kind switch; `keysForm()`, its keys, the simple ones in one form and each list or part in its own; `formOf()`, the simple keys in one form, with an optional helper line and reader, which the template card's slots use; `adder()`, an Add button                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
