## `src/templates/`: the template engine

[Templates](templates.md) is the language; this is how it is built.

- `expand.ts`: `expand(templates, instance, discovered, later)` returns `{ card, popups }` and touches nothing else. A name in `later`, a shipped template not loaded yet, is drawn as nothing and listed in `missing`, so one pass names every family a card still needs; a name in neither is an error. It checks each template's slots once (known kinds, lower-case names, no shape left unresolved), resolves each slot (the instance's value, else the discovered one, else the default), checks its kind and its fields, and renders the template's tree: `[[path]]`, with `*`, `?field` and `!field` projecting a path over a list, `each`/`as`, `if`/`unless`, nested `template:` with `slots:`, keys ending in `?`, lists spliced. A mistake is a `TemplateError` naming the template and the path. `toValue()` copies JSON-like data into a `Value`, so a TypeScript caller converts its interfaces once, without a cast. A fifth argument, a marking (`{ singles }`), makes the expansion write `_part`, the path of the part (`card/chips/#window`, the same path the outline and `valueAt()` use) on every item of a list with an id, on the card, and on each single part the marking names, never inside a fragment, and never where it would be added to a list. The Design tab's stage reads it; the cards carry it as `data-part` on what they draw (`ha/part.ts`) and take it as a key of every part, drawing nothing different. It checks a template's `retired` paths once (dotted slot paths, none of them declared), takes a value given for a retired path and ignores it, and allows `?field` and `!field` only over a list of objects.
- `changes.ts`: `applyChanges(template, changes)` lays the home's changes over a shipped template (set, remove, insert, move, by a path of keys and `#<id>`s) and says which are changed or gone, judged against the shipped template; `isChange()` checks a change's shape for its op; `baseOf()` is the hash a change's `base` holds, of what it touches; `nodeHash()` is the stable hash under it; `changesOf(base, edited)` works out the changes from a shipped template to an edit of it. An `id:` on a list item is a control key to `expand()`, so no card sees it; `ids.test.ts` holds every part of a shipped card or pop-up to one, unique in its list.
- `ids.ts`, `ids.json`, `ids-main.ts`: every released part path, and the retired ones; `pnpm run fix:ids` (part of `pnpm fix`) adds new parts, and `ids.test.ts` fails on one gone without being retired, and on a shipped id that starts with `my-`, the prefix of the ids the panel gives.
- `discover.ts`: `discover(template, area, registries)` fills the slots that have a rule, from the areas, devices, entities and states it is given; with no area, only the `scope: all` rules. It is pure too; the template card hands it `hass`'s registries.
- `discover.ts` also holds the filters (`matches()` reads the entry, the state's attributes and the device), the label override (`discoverSlot()` looks for `mnml_<slot>` before the rules), `fromDevice(spec, device, area, registries)`, an `object` slot filled from a device given by the slot's field rules, as its anchor or its label fills it, which the card editor's **Use another** writes, and `relativesOf()` and `deviceName()`, a device's `via_device` relatives and its name as Home Assistant shows it.
- `explain.ts`: `explain(template, area, registries)` returns, per slot with a rule, the value and the steps taken (`Step`: the slot's field it is for, `''` for the slot itself, the rule in words, the entities that matched, best first, the ones picked, the ones tied with the best, for an anchored rule the devices that hold a match and the ones taken, the near misses and why they missed), and for an empty slot a reason. For an `object` slot, `devices` are the devices (`DeviceFit`: id, name, area's name) that the slot's own anchor or label found and that fill it, and `device` the one chosen; a step inside the slot offers none. It runs `discover()`'s own code with a recorder, so the two cannot disagree.
- `corpus.ts`, `corpus/`, `corpus-main.ts`: the discovery corpus. `corpus/*.json` are registries (areas, devices, entities, states): `tidy`, `messy`, `labelled`, `systems` and `devices`, written by hand to hold what real homes do (two matches for one slot, a hidden entity, a device with no area, an entity whose own area beats its device's; in `labelled`, the `mnml_` labels a user puts on entities; in `systems`, no areas and the devices of the system integrations, Proxmox, UniFi, Tailscale and the media servers; in `devices`, a room's richer devices: a robot vacuum and its dock, an air conditioner, a radiator's thermostat and a heater with no device, metered and plain plugs, a 3D printer, a speaker and a washer), and `demo`, a snapshot of the throwaway Home Assistant (`pnpm run corpus:demo`, which only ever reads a local instance; `tools/snapshot.ts` keeps what discovery and the builder read: the attributes the rules filter on, `hvac_modes` among them, and a person's `device_trackers`, a device's maker, model, entry type, `via_device` link and labels, an entity's own name). `corpus/expected.json` is what every shipped template discovers in every area of every home; `corpus.test.ts` fails when that changes, and `pnpm run accept:corpus` accepts the change, to be read in the diff; it is not part of `pnpm fix`, so a change in what discovery finds is always a decision. `tools/snapshot.ts` keeps what discovery reads of a state: `hvac_modes`, `source_type`, `device_trackers`, and the devices' maker, model, `entry_type`, `via_device_id` and labels.
- `shipped.ts`: `readTemplates()` reads `templates/*.yaml` with `yaml`, refusing a name defined twice; `SHIPPED` is what it read, for the generator and the tests. `familyNames()` and `readFamily()` read one file, a family, at a time, its shapes resolved; `readShapes()` reads `templates/shapes.yaml`, which is no family.
- `slot-shapes.ts`: `withShapes(name, template, shapes)` writes out every slot and field that names a shape ([Shapes](templates.md#writing-a-template)): the shape's spec with the slot's own keys over it, a list of it for `kind: objects`, and the fields it changes. It leaves a template that names no shape as it is, and a mistake is a `TemplateError` naming the template and the slot. The template types as written, before their shapes are resolved, are `WrittenSlot` and `WrittenTemplate` in `src/contract/templates.ts`. It leaves a template that names no shape as it is, and a slot or field that is not a mapping to the engine's own checks; a mistake names the template, the slot and the shapes it goes through.
- `families.ts`: the families as the browser gets them: `COMMON`, the shared fragments of `common.yaml`; `OWNER`, the family of every other name; `SHAPES`, the literal card type and `grid_options` of each family template, for sizing a card before its family arrives; `SLOT_SHAPES`, the shipped slot shapes, which the store resolves the home's own templates with; and `loadFamily(family)`. In Node it reads the YAML; in the bundle a rolldown plugin in `src/build/bundle.ts` replaces it, with `COMMON`, `OWNER`, `SHAPES` and `SLOT_SHAPES` as data, every family's JSON file written with its shapes resolved, and a `loadFamily()` that fetches the family's JSON file next to the bundle, so the browser carries no YAML parser.
- `detach.ts`: `detach(use, templates, taken)` writes a template use out: what the used template draws, its slots replaced by what the use gave them (a reference to a slot of the template around stays one), its conditions and loops renamed to match, its pop-ups returned. It gives up on what cannot be written out, and `detach.test.ts` writes out every use of every shipped template and checks that the demo home draws as before.
- `roles.ts`: `rolesOf(templates)`, each template a tile, a pop-up or a part ([Roles](templates.md#roles)), for the library and the gallery.
- `dashboard.ts`: `expandDashboard(templates, config)` expands every template card of a dashboard and gathers their pop-ups into its popups card, in document order: what a dashboard of templates draws, without a browser. An instance's layout keys (`grid_options`, `visibility`, `view_layout`, `layout_options`, `card_mod`) stay on the card it expands to; its `area` is not read, so the card has only what the instance spells.
- `overrides.ts`: `overridesOf(found, values)`, what a card's values change of what discovery found: the editor and the builder both write it.

The template format's types are `src/contract/templates.ts`, part of the public interface beside `cards.ts`.

## `src/home/`: the home generator

A whole dashboard from one typed object: [The home dashboard](home.md) says what it draws.

- `types.ts`: `Home` and its parts (`Room`, `Lights`, `Heating`, `Ac`, `Person`, `Car`, `System` and the rest), every entity spelled with its domain's id type, and the frame (`Dashboard`, `Card`). It is public interface, as the contract is. `HOME_KEYS`, `ROOM_KEYS`, `PERSON_KEYS`, `CAR_KEYS`, `SYSTEM_KEYS` and `SECTION_TITLES_KEYS` name the keys of `Home`, `Room`, `Person`, `Car`, `System` and `SectionTitles`, whose sections, like `order`, are the builder's `SectionKey`s, each a `Record<keyof T, true>`, so the compiler rejects a table that misses a key or names one the type lacks; `interface.json` records them. It records the keys of those six types only, not of the types inside them (`Lights`, `Vacuum`, `Proxmox`, ...): a change to one of those fails a home's type check where the home spells it, and the release notes name it by hand.
- `slots.ts`: one function per subject from its part of the home to its template's slots, in snake_case: `roomSlots()`, `proxmoxSlots()`, `systemSlots()`, `glancesSlots()`, `headingSlots()` and `snake()`, which the others, a person, a car and the systems, take as they are. It computes only what a template cannot: the room's joined, sorted batteries, the server's message sources, the system's firmware per room, and the home-wide lists of the Glances strip. A list that only gathers a field of another slot's list is a projection in the template (`[[devices.*.update]]`), not a slot.
- `plan.ts`: `homePlan(home)`, the home as a builder's `Plan` with every choice spelled (the Glances strip, each room, person and system tile by its slots, the cars by key, the sections' titles as their looks, `popupOpen` as `open`), and `systemChoices(home)`, the system tiles in their order, which `problems()` reads too.
- `view.ts`: `build(home)`, `homePlan(home)` drawn by `dashboardOf()` with no registries, so nothing is discovered: one `sections` view of `custom:mnml-template-card` instances, every slot spelled and no `area`, the Glances strip and the sections one under another, and the popups card; `drawn(home)`, the same dashboard as the templates expand it, which is what a tool that checks entity ids reads. It expands with the shipped templates only; a home's shared templates are seen by the cards, not by `drawn()`.
- `problems.ts`: `problems(home)`, what would break the dashboard without failing its build: a hash opened that no pop-up defines, a hash defined or producible twice, a key that is no URL fragment, a subnet that is no IPv4 range. A home's tests assert it is empty.

## `src/builder/`: the dashboard builder

What the panel's builder makes a dashboard from. It is pure: it reads the home's registries and the templates it is given, so it runs in the panel and in Node alike.

- `plan.ts`: `planFrom(recipe, registries, templates)` refills a dashboard template in a home: the areas that are rooms where the rooms section's template draws, every person, the system section's templates whose entities discovery finds, no car, and the sections' looks; `DEFAULT_RECIPE` is the shipped one, and `defaultPlan(registries, templates)`, the quick start, is it refilled: the areas that are rooms where the room template draws something beyond the area's name and icon, in the order Home Assistant lists them; every `person` entity; each of `SYSTEM_TEMPLATES` whose required slots discovery fills over the whole home; pop-ups that unfold on tablet and desktop. `areaKinds(registries)` tells each area's kind from one table of marks on its entities (platform, domain, device class, entity category, and for a temperature or humidity sensor that a device measures it, a device that is no service, or that it is the area's own): `room` when it holds something a room shows, otherwise `phones`, `system` or `empty`, by its devices; `unplaced(registries)` counts the devices in no area that hold something a room shows ([Building a dashboard](editors.md#building-a-dashboard)). The room test (`MARKS`, `areaKinds()`, `unplaced()`) reads each area's entities against one table of marks; a `device_tracker` moves only with `source_type: gps`.
- `person.ts`: `personOf(registries, entity)`, a person's slots: the key from the entity id, and one device per tracker in the person's `device_trackers` that the companion app (`mobile_app`) made, with the app's sensors on that device by their entity ids' endings (`_battery_level`, `_battery_state`, `_connection_type`, `_ssid`, `_storage`, `_focus`, `_activity`, `_location_permission`). A tracker that lacks one of them is left out, and a person with none is the person entity alone.
- `customized.ts`: from a card its editor changed back to the plan: `roomFrom()` (the area picked, the overrides), `personFrom()` and `systemFrom()` (only what differs from what MNML finds, by `overridesOf()`), and `carFrom()`, a spelled row staying spelled (the key out of the slots, or no car without one that is a name).
- `recipe.ts`: `recipeOf(plan, templates, shipped)`, a dashboard template from a plan: the sections it has (one with something, or with a look), their looks, the system templates chosen, the openings, and every template it uses, inside others too, that is not the shipped one as shipped, whole; `recipeText()` writes it under `mnml_dashboard:`; `readRecipe(text, shipped)` reads one, refusing a dashboard's configuration, a set of templates, an unknown section, or a section template neither shipped nor bundled, with the reason; `renamedRecipe()` follows the names its templates come in under.
- `dashboard.ts`: `dashboardOf(plan, registries, templates)`, one `sections` view with a heading and the cards of each part that has any (Rooms, People, Garage, System, in the plan's `order`), each heading and template from the section's look, and the popups card. The Glances strip comes first, across the view, then the sections, one under another. A spelled choice is its slots alone. A room is its `area`, discovered live, with its overrides; a person is `personOf()` with the overrides over it; a car is its slots and key. `roomCard()`, `personCard()`, `carCard()` and `systemCard()` make each card alone, for the builder's rows. A system template without overrides is the template alone and discovers live; with them, it holds what discovery found when the plan was built, and the overrides over it, since a card that spells slots does not discover. Every card holds only the slots and fields its template declares, a retired one dropped too; an area room left with none has no `slots`. `roomCard()`, `personCard()` and `carCard()` take the templates as an optional last argument.

## `custom_components/mnml/`: the integration

One config entry (`single_config_entry`), no devices and no entities. Its flow asks the two options, the glass design and MNML as the default theme, and the options form asks them again.

| File                   | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `__init__.py`          | `async_setup_entry()`: the stores, then the websocket commands, the frontend, the panel, the theme and the repairs, the default theme, the options listener; `async_unload_entry()` takes the bundle and the panel off the pages and clears the repairs; `async_remove_entry()` deletes the theme and gives the default theme back. `MnmlData` (whether the glass design is on) is the entry's runtime data; the options listener swaps the theme when the design changes. The default theme option is what is wanted, and the entry's data keeps what was last applied (`applied_default_theme`): at setup and on every change of the options, `async_sync_default()` makes MNML the default theme, or gives the default back, when the two differ, and makes it the default only while Home Assistant loads MNML's theme. So an answer of the setup form, or an option turned on before the theme loads, takes effect at the first setup that finds the theme, and a start with nothing changed leaves a default chosen since in Home Assistant alone                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `frontend.py`          | `loader_url(www)`, `/mnml-files/mnml-cards-loader.js?v=<first 8 of the sha256 of the loader and the bundle>`, which fails setup with `ConfigEntryError`, naming what is missing, when the loader, the bundle, the panel or one of the two themes (`mnml.yaml`, `mnml-flat.yaml`) is not built; `async_register_frontend()` serves `www/` at `/mnml-files/` with long cache headers (once per Home Assistant run) and adds the loader to every page with `add_extra_js_url`. The URL comes off the pages on unload, and when a later step of setup fails                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `theme.py`             | `write_theme()` writes a built theme to `themes/mnml-integration/mnml.yaml`, atomically, when it differs; `async_install_theme(glass=)` chooses `www/mnml.yaml` or, flat, `www/mnml-flat.yaml`, and then reloads themes, and when Home Assistant does not load a theme named MNML from it (no `themes` include, an include of another folder, or `!include_dir_named`, which cannot hold it) takes the folder away again, so the configuration stays valid. A reload that fails is tried again without the folder: when that one succeeds, the file was the cause and stays away; when it fails too, the cause is elsewhere (an error in `configuration.yaml`), so the file is written back, the failure is logged and no repair is raised, and the theme loads at Home Assistant's next reload or restart; `theme_loaded()` says whether Home Assistant holds a theme named MNML; `other_theme_files()` finds another file under `themes/` that defines MNML, the standalone theme from HACS in `themes/mnml/` included; `async_apply_default()` sets MNML as the default theme in light and dark mode, or, turned off, gives back each mode MNML still holds (`none`), and logs a change Home Assistant refuses rather than raising it; `async_remove_theme()` deletes the folder and reloads themes, which also gives back a default that named MNML |
| `conflicts.py`         | `async_hand_loaded()`: the URL of a Lovelace resource, stored in the UI or in YAML, that loads `mnml-cards.js` from anywhere but `/mnml-files/`. It reads Lovelace's resource collection, which is not a promised API, and answers nothing when that collection is not what it expects                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `dashboards.py`        | `DashboardStore`: the dashboards the panel's builder made, in `.storage/mnml.dashboards`, by their `url_path`: each one's plan, its last save's time and user, and the version a rebuild replaced (its plan and its Lovelace configuration), which an undo restores. `DASHBOARD_STORE` is its key in `hass.data`, loaded beside the templates' store; one that cannot be read is logged and left out, and its commands answer `not_loaded`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `issues.py`            | The three repairs, raised or cleared on every setup: `theme_not_loaded`, `second_theme`, `hand_loaded_bundle`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `store.py`             | `TemplateStore`: the home's templates in `.storage/mnml.templates`, through Home Assistant's storage helper, each with its last save's time and user and its previous 10 versions; listeners are told after each write. `STORE` is its key in `hass.data`, loaded on the first setup of a run, before the cards are served, so a page that loads them finds the store ready. A store that cannot be read is logged and left out: setup goes on, the websocket answers `not_loaded`, and the cards draw the shipped templates                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `panel.py`             | `async_register_panel()`, the MNML panel at `/mnml` for admins, with the icon `mnml:mnml`, from `www/mnml-cards-panel.js` named by its content; `async_remove_panel()` on unload                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `websocket.py`         | `mnml/templates/subscribe` (every user: the set, then the set again after each save and delete), `save`, `delete` and `history` (admins), and `mnml/dashboards/list`, `save` and `delete` (admins: a plan of the shape of `isPlan()`, and the version it replaces, at a `url_path` of lower case letters and digits with a hyphen between them, as Home Assistant's own dashboards have, at most 512 kB each and 100 in all), registered once per run, with the shape checks of [Templates](templates.md#where-templates-live) and at most 500 templates                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `config_flow.py`       | The flow, whose one form asks Use the glass design (on) and Use MNML as the default theme (off), and the options form, which asks the same two                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `translations/en.json` | Every string Home Assistant shows: the flow, the option, the repairs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `brand/`               | The icons, drawn as `icon-light.svg` and `icon-dark.svg`; `pnpm icons` renders each to a PNG of 256 and 512 px with transparent corners: `icon.png` and `icon@2x.png` from the light one, `dark_icon.png` and `dark_icon@2x.png` from the dark one. Home Assistant serves them for the integration, the logo names falling back to the icon of the same theme, and HACS's brand check finds `icon.png`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

**Why a loader.** Home Assistant imports an extra module as soon as its page starts, before its app has installed the scoped custom-element registry it runs on. A card class declared before that extends the browser's own `HTMLElement` and cannot be constructed afterwards. So the page gets `mnml-cards-loader.js` (`src/cards/loader.ts`), which waits until `home-assistant` is defined (`src/cards/started.ts`) and then imports `mnml-cards.js` with its own `?v=`; on a page where Home Assistant already runs it imports at once. Before it waits, the loader registers the `mnml` icon set (`src/cards/iconset.ts`) in `window.customIcons`, as Home Assistant's frontend reads it: `mnml:mnml` is the logo's frame made square, with M and N on the first row and M and the corner on the second, one 24 px path in the colour of wherever it is drawn. Being early, it is there before the sidebar draws the panel's icon.

`/mnml-files/` and not `/mnml/`: the panel takes `/mnml`. `themes/mnml-integration/` and not `themes/mnml/`: HACS installs the standalone MNML Theme there. An update of the integration takes effect after a restart, as for any integration; a reload of the entry serves a rebuilt `www/` under a new `?v=`.

## `demo/`: the demo

- `home.ts`: `DEMO`, a home of nine rooms, Joe and Jane, two cars and the six systems, which draws every template. The demo integration supplies its climates, media players, calendars, camera, vacuum, weather, lock and the kitchen's lights, under their own ids.
- `main.ts` writes `out/demo.yaml`; `tools/dashboard.ts` saves the same dashboard as `mnml-demo` on the throwaway instance.
- `traits.ts`: each demo entity's name, icon (by state where it changes), unit, device class and reading, taken once from the home the demo was made from, with the same names and words scrubbed as in `home.ts`.
- `states.ts`: what makes the demo lived in: the rooms whose lights are off, the rooms heating, who is away, and a few states set outright (an open window, a low and a critical battery, an unlocked car, a stopped guest, a print running).
- `entities.ts`: `packageOf(home)`, a Home Assistant package of template entities, scenes, scripts, helpers and generic thermostats for every id the home draws that the demo integration does not supply, from the traits and the states, and a `customize` block that names and icons the demo integration's entities, the scenes and the thermostats (`customizeOf()`), which `tools/demo.ts` also writes to the registry of those that have an entry, since a card reads a registered entity's name from the registry; run, it writes `.ha/packages/demo.yaml` and copies the QR, map and 3D printer images to `.ha/www/`. `created()` lists the ids a package makes, and its test holds the two together. `tools/demo.ts` adds the people and their device trackers, home or away, the 3D printer's camera from its image, and to each numeric template sensor a display precision of as many decimals as its reading, renames what Home Assistant kept from an earlier run, removes the demo's entities the package does not make, and fails on an id another integration took first, which belongs in `SUPPLIED`.

## `src/build/`: the build

- `buildBundle(file)` is one rolldown build for the browser, of minified ES modules written beside `file`. Three entries keep fixed names: `mnml-cards.js`, the bundle (`src/cards/register.ts`); `mnml-cards-loader.js` (`src/cards/loader.ts`); and `mnml-cards-panel.js` (`src/panel/main.ts`), which the integration registers, and whose `yaml` package reaches no dashboard.
- **The card editors** (`src/editors/main.ts`) are a chunk of their own, `mnml-cards-editors-<hash>.js`, which nothing imports statically. The build fills the generated module `src/editors/where.ts` with its URL, and a card imports it from its `getConfigElement()` (`src/cards/edit.ts`). The URL is a module of its own on purpose: a browser keeps a failed dynamic import for the page, so a retry asks for the same file under a fresh URL, `?attempt=<n>`. The editors carry no YAML parser, since Home Assistant's own YAML tab covers YAML.
- **Shared chunks.** What several entries share is a chunk named by its content, `mnml-cards-<name>-<hash>.js`.
- **The literals are minified.** A plugin runs `minify-literals` (lightningcss for the styles, html-minifier-next for the markup) over every file under `src/` that holds a `css`, `html` or `svg` template.
- **The families.** `common.yaml` goes in as data. Every other family is written beside the bundle as `mnml-cards-<family>.json`, and the bundle names each by its content (`?v=<hash>`), since the integration serves them with long cache headers.
- **A build starts clean.** It first removes every file of the folder whose name starts with the bundle's stem (`mnml-cards`), so no chunk of an earlier build stays beside the new ones.
- **Each map is named by its content.** Every file has its source map beside it, sources included, so a browser's developer tools show the TypeScript and a stack trace names it. The file's last line is `//# sourceMappingURL=<file>.map?v=<hash>`, the map's own hash. The files are served with long cache headers, so a fixed name could pair a new file with an older map; a new map is a new URL. Its paths are relative to this repository (`src/...`), and a dependency's start at its package (`node_modules/lit-html/...`) wherever the package manager keeps it, so a build inside a parent workspace writes the maps a checkout of its own does.
- `node src/build/main.ts [out]` writes them into `out` (resolved from the working directory), the bundle under the name `src/build/names.ts` gives; `pnpm run build:frontend` gives it `custom_components/mnml/www/`, and a project that holds MNML as a submodule builds into its own folder.
- `node src/theme/main.ts [out]` writes `mnml.yaml` (glass) and `mnml-flat.yaml` there, after every contrast claim of both holds; `pnpm run build:theme` gives it the same folder. `pnpm build` runs both.

## Releases

`.github/workflows/check.yml` runs on every pull request and every push to `main`, as jobs that run side by side, each on its own runner: `lint` (oxfmt, oxlint, markdownlint, knip), `typescript` (vitest), `python` (ruff, ruff format, mypy), `pytest`, `hassfest`, `floor` (the Python tests on the oldest Home Assistant supported) and `hacs` (HACS's validation). Together they run every step of `pnpm check`, and `build.test.ts` fails when a step of it is in no job. A tag `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, one release at a time: the same checks, by calling `check.yml`, and beside them the build job, a check that the tag is `v` and the version in `manifest.json`, a check that the tag is annotated, the release notes, `pnpm build` and `pnpm zip`; once both pass, a GitHub release with `mnml.zip` attached. `hacs.json` sets `zip_release`, so HACS unpacks `mnml.zip` into `custom_components/mnml/`; a hand install does the same.

HACS's validation runs every check, its brand check satisfied by `brand/icon.png`; hassfest checks the manifest and `build.test.ts` holds `hacs.json`. Every action is pinned to a commit, so a moved tag cannot change what CI runs; the build job reads the repository only, without credentials left on disk, and only the publish job, which runs no repository code, may write. A tag with a `-` (`v0.2.0-rc.1`) makes a prerelease, which HACS offers only to those who ask for it. The publishing step skips a release that already exists, so a release that failed half way is re-run as it is.

**The release notes** are written by hand and completed by the release. The maintainer writes them as the annotated tag's message: what changed, and for each part of the public interface removed, renamed or changed in meaning, a line on how to migrate. The tag is made with `git tag -a --cleanup=verbatim vX.Y.Z` (with `-F` for a message in a file): by default `git tag` drops every line that starts with `#`, and a Markdown heading with it. The build job writes `notes.md`: that message, then `node tools/notes.ts <previous tag>`, the entries of `interface.json` removed, changed (a key's or a slot's kind, required flag, values or default) and added since the previous tag, read with `git show <tag>:interface.json`. The previous tag of a release is the last `v*` tag before it, and for a stable release the last stable one, a prerelease skipped (`git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match 'v*' --exclude '*-*' "$TAG^"`), so that its notes cover every change since the release before it rather than since its last release candidate. A tag that records no `interface.json` is said to have none, a tag whose record is of another format is said to need comparing by hand, with nothing listed, and the first tag has no diff. Its checkout fetches the whole history and every tag for this. The publish job receives `notes.md` as an artifact and the previous tag as the build job's output, and creates the release with `--notes-file notes.md --generate-notes --notes-start-tag <previous tag>`, so the pull requests GitHub lists, since that same tag, follow the notes.

Dependabot (`.github/dependabot.yml`) opens a pull request each week for the Python tools (uv), the Node packages (pnpm) and the pinned actions; `pytest-homeassistant-custom-component` and `home-assistant-frontend` move together in one. Its security updates bump only the vulnerable package itself, so a package Home Assistant pins exactly, such as PyJWT or cryptography, is fixed by the weekly bump of `pytest-homeassistant-custom-component`, which brings the Home Assistant that pins a patched version. Those packages serve the tests only; the integration requires none. `.github/workflows/dependabot.yml` turns on auto-merge for Dependabot's patch and minor updates, so they squash into `main` once the checks pass. It names the two kinds it merges rather than the one it skips, so an update whose kind it cannot read waits too, as a major one does; and it acts only when Dependabot both opened the pull request and pushed to it.

## The repository

- **`main` takes changes only through pull requests.** A ruleset requires a pull request whose checks, the jobs of `check.yml`, pass, merges it by squashing, keeps the history linear, and refuses a force-push or a deletion of `main`. A merged branch is deleted.
- **Release tags stay put.** A second ruleset refuses to move or delete a `v*` tag, so a release always names the commit CI built.
- **The wiki is made from `docs/`.** `.github/workflows/wiki.yml` runs `tools/wiki.ts` on every push to `main` that changes `README.md` or `docs/`, and pushes the result to the wiki: each doc becomes a page named after its title and the README the Home page; a link between docs becomes a link between pages, and a link to any other file an absolute link to GitHub; a sidebar lists the pages, and each page names the file it is made from. The docs stay the source, written and reviewed with the code; the wiki is for reading.
- **Reports.** `SECURITY.md` sends a vulnerability to GitHub's private advisories. An issue opens from a bug or a feature form (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`), and a pull request from a checklist (`.github/pull_request_template.md`).

## Tests

- **The integration's tests** are in `tests/`, beside `plans.json`, the example plans both `src/contract/builder.test.ts` and `tests/test_dashboards.py` judge, on `pytest-homeassistant-custom-component`, which runs a real Home Assistant in each test, with `home-assistant-frontend` for the frontend it depends on. The fixtures in `conftest.py` give each test a `www/` of its own (`const.WWW` is patched), a config folder with the themes include, `setup_mnml()` and `themes()` (the frontend's `frontend/get_themes`). `pnpm test` runs them, after vitest, on the Home Assistant that `pytest-homeassistant-custom-component` brings; `pnpm run test:python-floor` on the oldest supported (2026.10.0b0, the first with probatio, the validation library that replaces voluptuous), with its own harness and frontend.
- **The TypeScript tests**, `*.test.ts`, sit next to what they cover and run on vitest, in the two projects of `vitest.config.ts`: `node`, for the contract, the engine, the generator, the builder, the theme, the build, the tools and the demo; and `browser`, on jsdom, for the cards, `src/ha/`, the store, the editors, the panel and `src/test/`. `test` comes from vitest, assertions from `node:assert/strict`. vitest runs each file in a module state of its own, so a test that needs an empty store or registry is a file of its own; `template-failure.test.ts` and `template-card-failure.test.ts` replace `families.ts` with `vi.mock()`, so a card and the template card's gallery meet a family that cannot be loaded.
- **Elements are mounted** with `src/test/render.ts`: `define()` defines a tag once, `mounted()` puts an element in the document and waits for its update, then gives its shadow root, `text()` reads the text a user sees, and `drawn()` renders a template into a box of its own, and `styled()` renders one under a set of styles, for a test that reads a computed style, and removes its hosts after each test. A test queries the shadow root and sends real DOM events.
- `src/test/fake-hass.ts` is a fake connection for the store: `fakeStore()` answers `mnml/templates/subscribe` with `kept` (or as a home without the integration when it is unset), refuses with `refuse`, sends a save with `keep()`, records each message and each subscription's options, and reconnects.
- `styles.test.ts` asserts that every `--mnml-*` variable a card reads has a fallback, so the cards work under any theme.
- `editors/cards.test.ts` and `editors/form.test.ts` send every card the demo draws, and every example card, through its editor's description and through Home Assistant's form data, section by section and part by part, and want each back unchanged, key order included; the type checker holds each card's and part's structure to every key of its contract type. `editors/labels.test.ts` fails while a key of a structure the editors draw has no label, or the table labels a structure, a key, a help or a kind that is not there.
- `src/cards/templates.test.ts` expands every shipped template from its `example`, and again with only its required slots, and gives each MNML card it draws, at any depth, to that card's `setConfig()`: a key a card does not know fails wherever an example reaches it, and a branch no example fills goes unchecked. It also holds every object slot to its declared `fields:`, and every path into one to a declared field. `src/templates/docs.test.ts` fails when `docs/templates.md` misses a template, a slot or a field.
- `examples/cards.yaml` is a hand-written configuration of every card, on the `demo` integration's entities and the template entities of `examples/fixtures.yaml`. `tools/` installs it on a throwaway Home Assistant and looks at it under both themes. `examples/templates.yaml` is a second view, rooms placed by `area`, which `tools/areas.ts` fills by moving demo entities into two areas.

### The throwaway Home Assistant

It runs in Docker, from `.ha/` (git-ignored), with `custom_components/mnml/` of this tree mounted read-only, and has no tie to a home. Then:

```bash
pnpm demo
```

`tools/up.ts` does the whole round, and runs again as often as wanted:

1. writes `.ha/configuration.yaml` the first time (the `demo` integration, the themes folder, the packages), and copies `recipes/messages.yaml` and `examples/fixtures.yaml` into `.ha/packages/`;
2. writes the demo's package with `node demo/entities.ts`, and builds `custom_components/mnml/www/` (`pnpm build`);
3. starts `ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:beta` afresh (the beta channel, while the oldest Home Assistant supported is a beta) as the container `mnml-ha`, published on `127.0.0.1:8124` only (`pnpm demo` takes a name and a port, `node tools/up.ts mnml-ha-glass 8125`, for a second one beside it), and waits until Home Assistant answers;
4. on a `.ha/` with no owner yet, onboards it: the owner `demo`, password `demo`, and a long-lived token written to `.env` (git-ignored) with `HA_URL=http://localhost:8124` (or the port given); then waits until Home Assistant is running;
5. runs `tools/demo.ts` (the demo's people, device trackers, camera, names, icons and display precisions), `tools/areas.ts` (the two areas the examples' templates view places rooms in), `tools/ids.ts` (every id in the examples and the demo exists), and `tools/dashboard.ts`, which removes what an older install put in `.ha/` (the `/local/mnml` resources, `www/mnml-cards*`, `themes/mnml.yaml`), adds the MNML entry or reloads it, saves the templates of `examples/home-templates.yaml` to the store, removes the `mnml-templates` dashboard an older install made, saves the `mnml-examples` and `mnml-demo` dashboards, and reloads the themes.

The loader's address carries a digest of the files, taken when the integration starts, so a build the running demo has not seen is served under the old address: restart the demo (`pnpm demo`) or reload MNML's entry after a build, then reload the page. A page opened before an update asks for an editor file that is gone, and says to reload the page.

The tools reach it over Home Assistant's websocket through `home-assistant-js-websocket` (`tools/socket.ts`), and refuse an `HA_URL` that is not local (`tools/env.ts`), so one run from another project's folder cannot reach a home with that project's token. `docker stop mnml-ha` stops it; deleting `.ha/` and `.env` starts over. Then, by hand, each in Playwright's Chromium (`tools/browser.ts`, installed once with `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`), signed in with the token:

```bash
pnpm look           # out/look/: the default theme and MNML, light and dark, phone and desktop
pnpm walk           # the panel, walked through: edit, save, reset, new, duplicate, delete, build a dashboard
pnpm videos         # out/videos/: five silent .webm tutorials, with captions, a visible cursor and click rings
pnpm screenshots    # docs/screenshots/: the demo for the README in the glass design, light and dark, six pop-ups and the panel, then the desktop in the flat design (through the options); tools/split.ts joins each desktop's light and dark diagonally into desktop.png and flat-desktop.png
```

`pnpm look` fails on any error card on the examples' cards and templates views, on a card of the examples whose editor cannot be opened or opens without a form (it mounts each inside `home-assistant`, whose context Home Assistant's pickers read), on a panel that lists no template or a shipped template whose builder does not open or shows a problem, and on a demo pop-up that opens nothing, has no header or shows a blank body. The panel and the demo it checks under MNML, light and dark, opening each of the demo's 51 pop-ups by its hash. The screenshots are read by eye: under the default theme each card keeps its hairline edge and its pills.

`pnpm videos` records the demo and the panel with Playwright's video recorder: a tour of the dashboard, building a dashboard, editing a shipped template, making a template and the phone layout. It needs the demo running (`pnpm demo`), draws a cursor and captions over the page since the videos have no sound, and leaves the demo as it found it. The videos stay in `out/`, which git ignores.

`pnpm walk` drives the panel on a desktop: it opens `room`, picks a part, edits a slot's label, sees the slot marked changed and the change counted in the header, saves, and finds `room` customised in the library; resets it to shipped and saves; makes a new template and saves it; duplicates it and sees the copy open under its own name; leaves another new template unsaved and finds its name free again; and deletes the first. Then it forgets every dashboard MNML built, finds the offer to build one, makes one by Quick start and opens it (template cards, no error card), rebuilds it with a new title and a room fewer, undoes the rebuild, shares it (no area or person in the text), forgets it with Delete it too, and makes it again from the shared text, which draws its rooms with no error card. It fails on a step that does not hold, and on a page error from MNML's files.

## Tooling

**Oxc for TypeScript, ruff and mypy for Python.**

- `oxlint`, with `typeAware` and `typeCheck` through `oxlint-tsgolint`, lints and reports the TypeScript diagnostics. There is no `tsc` and no `typescript` package.
- `oxfmt` formats; `knip` finds dead code; `rolldown` bundles the elements, and `minify-literals` minifies their templates; `vitest` runs the TypeScript tests, the elements' on jsdom.
- `ruff` lints and formats the Python, `mypy --strict` type checks it, and hassfest, Home Assistant's own validator, checks the integration in Docker (`ghcr.io/home-assistant/hassfest`, `linux/amd64`). HACS's validation reads the GitHub repository, so it runs in CI only.
- There are no git hooks. The bundle's one runtime dependency is Lit, which the build bundles; the integration has none; `home-assistant-js-websocket` is the tools' client for the throwaway Home Assistant.

| Tool         | Configuration                           | Rules of the house                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| oxlint       | `oxlint.config.ts`                      | Every rule is an error (`denyWarnings`), and so is an unused disable directive. A rule that fights a convention is turned off in the config, with the reason written here, never in an inline directive. `no-console` and `no-await-in-loop` are off for `src/*/main.ts`, `demo/main.ts`, `demo/entities.ts` and `tools/*.ts`, the command lines, which print and run one step after another on purpose. `no-console` is off for `src/cards/parts/popup-registry.ts`, which reports a hash announced twice on the console, where a dashboard's author looks, for `src/store/store.ts`, which reports there a card that threw on a change of the store, changes kept in a shape it does not know, and a template of the home's own whose slot shapes could not be resolved, for `src/store/shipped.ts`, which reports a family that could not be loaded, and for their tests, `template-failure.test.ts` and `template-card-failure.test.ts`, which replace `console.error` to see those reports or keep them quiet |
| oxfmt        | `oxfmt.config.ts`                       | The defaults (100 columns, semicolons, trailing commas, sorted `package.json`) plus single quotes and sorted imports                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| markdownlint | `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`              | Every rule but MD013, line length: a paragraph is one line. `CLAUDE.md`, an `@AGENTS.md` include, is skipped, and so is `.github/pull_request_template.md`, which starts a pull request's description and so opens with a second-level heading                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| vitest       | `vitest.config.ts`                      | Two projects: `node`, and `browser` on jsdom, each with the folders its tests run in ([Tests](#tests)). `test` comes from vitest, assertions from `node:assert/strict`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| knip         | `knip.jsonc`                            | Fails on unused files, dependencies and exports. Don't export what only the same file uses. Entries: the four the browser loads (`src/cards/register.ts`, `src/cards/loader.ts`, `src/editors/main.ts`, `src/panel/main.ts`), the contract (`cards.ts`, `entities.ts`, `templates.ts`) and the home's types (`src/home/types.ts`), whose exports are for the projects that use MNML, the tests, `tools/*.ts` and `demo/*.ts`. `uv` is a binary it leaves alone                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ruff         | `pyproject.toml`                        | Every rule but `D` (the code has no comments, so no docstrings), `COM812` (it fights ruff's formatter) and `CPY001` (no copyright headers); in `tests/` also `S101` (pytest asserts), `PLR2004` (expected values are literals), `SLF001` and `ARG001` (fixtures, and Home Assistant's test internals). 100 columns, Python 3.14 syntax                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| mypy         | `pyproject.toml`                        | `strict`, over `custom_components/` and `tests/`, with `explicit_package_bases` since `custom_components/` has no `__init__.py`. Two overrides: `pytest_homeassistant_custom_component` ships no types, and `homeassistant.components.http` re-exports `StaticPathConfig`, which the oldest Home Assistant supported defines there itself                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| hassfest     | `manifest.json`, `translations/en.json` | Home Assistant's rules for an integration: the manifest's keys, the config flow, the translations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| tsconfig     | `tsconfig.json`                         | `src/`, `demo/`, `tools/` and `vitest.config.ts`. Strict, with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` but without `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: an optional key may hold `undefined`, which a card reads as absent. `experimentalDecorators` and `useDefineForClassFields: false` are Lit's decorators as Home Assistant writes them: a class field defined by the standard would shadow the accessor a decorator puts on the class. rolldown and vitest compile them; Node, which only strips types, runs no module that imports an element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

- **Markdown too.** oxfmt formats the docs and realigns a table's columns to their display width. Leave a table to `pnpm fix` rather than padding it by hand.
- **Ignored paths.** `ignorePatterns` keeps oxfmt off `uv.lock`, `.ha/`, `out/`, `.venv/` and `custom_components/mnml/www/`. All the tools honour `.gitignore`.
- **Dependencies.** `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `uv.lock` hold the exact versions; `pnpm install` and `uv sync` install them, and CI's `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `uv sync --locked` refuse a lock that has drifted. `packageManager` in `package.json` names the pnpm. pnpm runs a dependency's install script only when the project allows it, and this one allows none, so no dependency may rely on one.
